text:
maria_support: ACME reports that org admins can no longer provision new service tokens from the Console. The "Create token" button is greyed and network call to /v1/orgs/org-789/tokens returns 403. This started after their Okta SSO migration last night. Sample network error: 403 {"error":"insufficient_scope", "required":"tokens.create"}
shawn_eng: do we have the request trace id or network payload from their devtools? also which admin role do they have (org-admin vs project-admin)?
maria_support: they confirmed org-admin in Console. Attached devtools snippet: response headers include x-auth-scopes: client:read,org:members — looks like create scope got trimmed. no trace id in screenshot but timestamp is 2026-02-18T22:03:10Z.
sara_ops: idp_sync_bot shows a SCIM sync and an attribute transform rule applied at 21:58 UTC during the migration. possible mapping removed a claim that converts Okta group -> Redwood org-admin?
idp_sync_bot: SCIM_SYNC event: complete; changes=groups:remove(OKTA:acme-admins) transforms_applied=true rule_id=okta-migration-2026-02
liam_sre: if SCIM removed the group membership, the token service policy evaluation would drop tokens.create scope. Can we confirm if the user was actually removed from the acme-admins group?
maria_support: customer confirms their admin user is still in Okta and acme-admins in Okta. Okta shows group present. SCIM sync log above implies it removed mapping to the Redwood group during transform.
shawn_eng: this sounds like claim/attribute normalization in the migration stripping the admin role claim before SCIM mapping. Repro steps we want from customer: 1) open devtools network tab -> replicate create token call -> copy request id & response headers 2) provide user subject (opaque id) used for SSO 3) paste partial id_token claims (masked) showing groups claim.
maria_support: asked customer for those items, they sent the response headers and a masked id_token claims array — groups only contains OKTA:acme-basic-users, not acme-admins.
liam_sre: quick mitigation: create token via server-side CLI using an existing org-admin API key (not SSO browser flow). endpoint: POST /v1/orgs/org-789/tokens with Authorization: Bearer <org-admin-key>. That bypasses the SSO-claim path and works for now. Customer confirmed CLI create succeeded.
sara_ops: long-term fix: revert transform rule that removed mapping or update claim mapping so Okta group name normalizes to acme-admins in id_token. Also trigger a full SCIM resync after mapping change.
shawn_eng: filing ENG-IDP-1123, priority P1 (customer-facing console blocking). Attach: id_token sample, SCIM sync event, network headers. Assign to identity team for mapping rollback.
maria_support: customer accepted CLI workaround for token creation. They've asked for ETA on fix, requested that we avoid further break during next SCIM run. I'll let them know once ENG-IDP-1123 gets a PR.
liam_sre: also adding an automated alert to detect when org-admin group membership is present in IdP but missing in SCIM mapping within 30m of a migration. Could reduce time-to-detect.
maria_support: thanks — closing loop with customer. INF-3456 created for follow-up and post-mortem.
